3.0.s.en: 1. The place and time of building the temple

3.0.0.en: 1 Then Solomon began to build the house of the LORD at Jerusalem in mount Moriah, where the LORD appeared unto David his father, in the place that David had prepared in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite. 2 And he began to build in the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign.

3.0.1.en: In our commentary on the Book of Exodus, chapter 25, we saw that Father Methodius says: [The Jews prophesied about our condition, but we prophesy about the heavenly things; since the tabernacle (or the temple) is a symbol of the Church, and the Church is a symbol of the heavenly things[1].]

3.0.2.en: Then Solomon began to build the house of the LORD at Jerusalem in mount Moriah, where the LORD appeared unto David his father, in the place that David had prepared in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite. [1]

3.0.3.en: This chapter is the only place in the Bible that declares that the site of the temple is Mount Moriah, on which Abraham offered his son Isaac as a burnt offering (Gen 22:2).

3.0.4.en: The temple was erected in the place where the first symbol, or practical sign, of the sacrifice of the Only-Begotten Son was fulfilled, which the Father offers for the salvation of humanity. This is the foundation and aim of the house of God: enjoying the sacrifice of redemption which the Lord Christ offered.

3.0.5.en: v Abraham, according to his faith, clung to the commandment of the Word of God, and with a ready mind offered a sacrifice to God, his only beloved son. For it pleased God to offer, on behalf of all his seed, His only beloved Son as a sacrifice for our redemption.

3.0.6.en: St. Irenaeus The choice of this place reveals God's view of His holy house in the midst of His people; it is the house of the Passover sacrifice that grants believers a joyful salvation.

3.0.7.en: Solomon did not need to study the site of the temple, for the site had already been determined for him beforehand (1 Chr 21:18; 22:1), to give him peace of mind, to save time, and to avoid long discussions among the leaders over choosing a suitable site for building it.

3.0.8.en: The site was fixed by a divine choice, and it was marked by the following:

3.0.9.en: a. It was in Jerusalem, because the Lord chose this city, and the Lord chose the place to put His name there. Also heaven has been called “Jerusalem which is above” (Gal 4:26).

3.0.10.en: b. On Mount Moriah, the mountain on which Abraham offered his son Isaac as a burnt offering (Gen 22:2). God gave Abraham a ram to offer in place of Isaac his son, and that was a type of the sacrifice of the Lord Christ. It was fitting that the house be built on the atoning sacrifice of Christ for the whole world.

3.0.11.en: c. In this place the Lord appeared to David and answered him with fire (1 Chr 21:18, 26), and there David offered an atoning sacrifice for the mistake he had committed.

3.0.12.en: d. David bought the place with his own money, and did not accept to offer the sacrifice on land given to him as a gift; he bought it through divine guidance.

3.0.13.en: e. The temple was erected on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite, so that the Gentiles might realize that God is the God of all humanity, and not exclusively of the Jews apart from the rest of the nations.

3.0.14.en: f. In Jewish tradition there is a story about the choice of this site. It is said that two brothers lived in this area, one married and the other single. The married brother, out of love for his brother and feeling that his brother needed much expense to prepare for marriage, used every night to carry grain from his storehouses and go secretly to put it in his brother's storehouses. The single brother felt that his brother, being married and supporting a family, needed much expense, so he did the same thing every night. In the morning each of them would find that his storehouses had not diminished but increased, because of the blessing of the Lord upon him. One night the two met, each carrying some of his grain to put in his brother's storehouses. Each asked the other what he was doing. The two embraced, and in their joy at their love for one another they wept. In this place, where brotherly love was revealed, God chose that His holy house be built, the house of divine and brotherly love.

3.1.0.en: And he began to build in the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign. [2]

3.1.1.en: As for the time of beginning the work, it is said that he did not begin the work until the fourth year of Solomon's reign [2]. The three years were not spent in discussions, for the site was determined and the architectural plan prepared. Rather, this huge work needed many preparations. The number of workers was very large, and some may have needed to finish what was in their hands in order to devote themselves entirely to this work.

3.2.s.en: 2. The dimensions of the temple and its adornment

3.2.0.en: 3 Now these are the things which Solomon founded for the building of the house of God. The length by cubits after the first measure was threescore cubits, and the breadth twenty cubits. 4 And the porch that was in the front of the house, the length of it was according to the breadth of the house, twenty cubits, and the height was an hundred and twenty: and he overlaid it within with pure gold. 5 And the greater house he cieled with fir tree, which he overlaid with fine gold, and set thereon palm trees and chains. 6 And he garnished the house with precious stones for beauty: and the gold was gold of Parvaim. 7 He overlaid also the house, the beams, the posts, and the walls thereof, and the doors thereof, with gold; and graved cherubims on the walls. 8 And he made the most holy house, the length whereof was according to the breadth of the house, twenty cubits, and the breadth thereof twenty cubits: and he overlaid it with fine gold, amounting to six hundred talents. 9 And the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. And he overlaid the upper chambers with gold.

3.2.1.en: Now these are the things which Solomon founded for the building of the house of God:

3.2.2.en: The length (by cubits after the first measure) was threescore cubits, and the breadth twenty cubits. [3]

3.3.0.en: And the porch that was in the front of the house, the length of it was according to the breadth of the house, twenty cubits, and the height was an hundred and twenty: and he overlaid it within with pure gold. [4]

3.3.1.en: The dimensions of the temple were handed over to Solomon by his father David, so there was no reason to change the dimensions.

3.3.2.en: It is noticed in the description of the temple that it is marked by a very great height in relation to its length and width: the length is like the width, twenty cubits, while its height is one hundred and twenty.

3.3.3.en: The height of the Holy Place was thirty cubits, while the porch that was before the Holy Place, and is not mentioned in the Book of Kings, was a separate, tall building in front of the Holy Place.

3.4.0.en: And the greater house he cieled with fir tree, which he overlaid with fine gold, and set thereon palm trees and chains. [5]

3.4.1.en: As for the adornment of the temple, the woodwork was exceedingly splendid, and yet it was overlaid with pure gold [5]. The great house was covered with fir wood, which he overlaid with pure gold, and set upon it palm trees and chains.

3.4.2.en: Concerning the wood used in the house of the Lord, Origen sees it as wood that does not rot, pointing to knowledge or to chastity that does not age[2] or decay.

3.4.3.en: As for the gold, as we have repeated before in our commentary on the Holy Bible, it points to heaven, the palm trees point to victory, and the chains point to unity and the binding of all together as with golden chains. This is what marks the Church of Christ, as she bears the heavenly mind, and always enjoys a life of victory in her struggle against the devil and sin, and as all her members are united together as one body to the Head, Christ, and His holy heavenly Bride.

3.4.4.en: Origen sees that gold is the faith that makes the heart a heaven, and so it points to the heavenly things, as it points to the saints as being a heaven in whose hearts God dwells.

3.4.5.en: He says: [If you believe, you offer your heart and mind as gold!... For this reason Moses, who represents the spiritual law, declares “Take ye from among you” (Ex 35:5). If you can take these things from among you, then they are within you. You can offer the Lord something of your feelings, and of your words, etc.[3].]

3.4.6.en: And Father Methodius sees that gold points to the life of virginity, for he says: [He commanded gold (that vessels be made of it inside the Holy of Holies) for two reasons: first, that it does not rust, and second, that its color is to some extent close to the color of the sun. Thus it suits virginity, which bears nothing defiled or wrinkled, but always shines with the light of the Word. Through it we stand near to God, inside the Holy of Holies and before the veil, with hands undefiled like incense, we offer prayers to the Lord as a sweet and acceptable fragrance, in the (golden) censers of the twenty-four elders, which are the prayers of the saints[4].]

3.5.0.en: And he garnished the house with precious stones for beauty:

3.5.1.en: and the gold was gold of Parvaim. [6]

3.5.2.en: The gold was the gold of Parvaim, one of the best kinds of gold.

3.6.0.en: He overlaid also the house, the beams, the posts, and the walls thereof, and the doors thereof, with gold; and graved cherubims on the walls. [7]

3.7.0.en: He graved cherubim on the walls; the Holy of Holies represents the heavenly throne of God by the presence of the two figures of the cherubim, and the veil is adorned with cherubim [14] who will not allow entry to the throne of God to any but those who bear the heavenly marks; even the walls are adorned with cherubim, because the house of the Lord is a second heaven!

3.8.0.en: And he made the most holy house, the length whereof was according to the breadth of the house, twenty cubits, and the breadth thereof twenty cubits: and he overlaid it with fine gold, amounting to six hundred talents. [8]

3.9.0.en: And the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. And he overlaid the upper chambers with gold. [9]

3.9.1.en: The beams, the thresholds, the walls and the doors were overlaid with gold.

3.9.2.en: If the temple points to the heart of the believer, as the Apostle Paul says: “Ye are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwelleth in you” (1 Cor 3:16), and gold points to the heavenly things, then it befits the believer that all his inner life and conduct bear a heavenly mark.

3.9.3.en: Likewise the Holy of Holies, whose length is like its breadth, twenty cubits, is all overlaid with gold. Even the nails were of gold, and also its upper chambers, or its ceiling, were overlaid with gold.

3.9.4.en: The temple was adorned with precious stones as a symbol of heaven, since all its walls and gates and foundations are adorned with precious stones and pearls (Rev 21:18-21).

3.10.s.en: 3. The two cherubim in the Holy of Holies

3.10.0.en: 10 And in the most holy house he made two cherubims of image work, and overlaid them with gold. 11 And the wings of the cherubims were twenty cubits long: one wing of the one cherub was five cubits, reaching to the wall of the house: and the other wing was likewise five cubits, reaching to the wing of the other cherub. 12 And one wing of the other cherub was five cubits, reaching to the wall of the house: and the other wing was five cubits also, joining to the wing of the other cherub. 13 The wings of these cherubims spread themselves forth twenty cubits: and they stood on their feet, and their faces were inward.

3.10.1.en: And in the most holy house he made two cherubims of image work, and overlaid them with gold. [10]

3.10.2.en: Since the word “cherub” means “knowledge”, Origen sees that the two cherubim are described as golden because they point to the abundance of (heavenly) knowledge[5].

3.11.0.en: And the wings of the cherubims were twenty cubits long: one wing of the one cherub was five cubits, reaching to the wall of the house: and the other wing was likewise five cubits, reaching to the wing of the other cherub. [11]

3.12.0.en: And one wing of the other cherub was five cubits, reaching to the wall of the house: and the other wing was five cubits also, joining to the wing of the other cherub. [12]

3.12.1.en: If the length of the wings of the two cherubim together is twenty cubits, five cubits for each wing, then the two wings are stretched out to occupy the whole width of the Holy of Holies, as though the Holy of Holies represents heaven and none is in it but one who bears the mark of heaven. It befits all people, when they meet the Lord, to enjoy the heavenly marks, and for dust to have no place in their hearts.

3.13.0.en: The wings of these cherubims spread themselves forth twenty cubits: and they stood on their feet, and their faces were inward. [13]

3.13.1.en: Before the building of the temple the two cherubim were on the cover of the ark of the covenant, and their size was relatively small. But after the temple was built, their size became large. Each wing extended five cubits.

3.13.2.en: The two cherubim stood, the wing of each touching the wing of the other, and the other wing touching the wall. So the extent of the four outspread wings reaches 20 cubits, that is, the width of the Holy of Holies [8, 12-13]. Their faces were turned inward toward the ark of the covenant. They appear as two servants of the invisible God, as though they invite all believers, Levitical priests and people, to join them in worshipping God, and not to worship them.

3.14.0.en: And he made the vail of blue, and purple, and crimson, and fine linen, and wrought cherubims thereon. [14]

3.14.1.en: The veil of the temple screens the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies. This veil reveals the need of humanity, even of those who worship God, for reconciliation with God, so that they may pass over into the heavenly things. This was fulfilled by the Cross of the Lord Christ, where the veil of the temple was rent, not by a human hand, but by the work of the Savior Himself.

3.14.2.en: The veil was made of different materials and various colors: blue, purple, crimson and fine linen [14]. The blue points to heaven; purple is worn by kings, crimson is the color of blood, and the white linen points to purity and cleanness. So it befits the believer to bear the heavenly mark, and to walk as a king with authority who does not fear the powers of darkness, enjoying the blood of the Lord Christ that forgives sins, and living in purity and chastity!

3.14.3.en: We have previously spoken of what each of the blue, the purple, the crimson and the linen symbolizes, in the commentary on Exodus chapter 25:

3.14.4.en: Origen sees that purple points to the radiance of love[6], and also points to fire[7]. The true Christian bears fire in his heart, the fire of the Holy Spirit, who lights up the way and burns the thorns that choke the soul.

3.14.5.en: Crimson points to the blood of the Lord Christ the Savior, for the crimson that we offer is our witness to Him unto blood, as the Apostle says: “For thy sake we are killed all the day long”; crimson pointed to martyrdom, whether by the shedding of the blood of believers in the ages of martyrdom, or by the life of daily mortification for the sake of the Lord.

3.14.6.en: The twined byssus (linen): since byssus points to the body, its being twined means being under control and restraint[8], as the Apostle says: “I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection” (1 Cor 9:27). Every struggle to control the body and master it in Christ Jesus is an offering to the house of the Lord.

3.15.0.en: Also he made before the house two pillars of thirty and five cubits high, and the chapiters that were on the top of them were five cubits. [15]

3.16.0.en: And he made chains, as in the oracle, and put them on the heads of the pillars; and made an hundred pomegranates, and put them on the chains. [16]

3.17.0.en: And he reared up the pillars before the temple, one on the right hand, and the other on the left; and called the name of that on the right hand Jachin, and the name of that on the left Boaz. [17]

3.17.1.en: Two pillars were set up before the temple, the height of each about 18 cubits (1 Kgs 7:15), and they were called Jachin and Boaz, meaning “the foundation, and the strength”.

3.17.2.en: Some see that these two pillars point to the house of David which the Lord established (2 Sam 7), and which continues by the power of the Lord.

3.17.3.en: There are chains on the heads of the two pillars that point to the unity of the whole nation, although it comprises the tribes.

3.17.4.en: If unity in the Old Testament was symbolized by chains binding the pillars, the Lord has given us His Body, so that all become different members in one body, having one Head, our Lord Jesus Christ.

3.18.0.en: With the privileges that Solomon enjoyed, such as obtaining wisdom and building the house of the Lord and others, matters in which he appears to have surpassed his father, these privileges condemn him all the more if he does not make good use of them. St. Mar Jacob of Serugh says that when the wise Solomon was radiant, God sent down fire upon his offering, a sign of His acceptance of him and His pleasure in him, and when he sacrificed to the demons, He cast him from before His face. In his answer to the question: Why did the Lord, who knows all things, choose Judas as His disciple? And why did He create Satan, who resists the divine truth? he said:

3.18.1.en: v If you say, why did the One who knows all choose him, when He knew that he was deceitful and untruthful?

3.18.2.en: He chose him when he was beautiful, pure and clean, with no blemish, gentle and upright, and full of love for the Son of God.

3.18.3.en: And after He chose him, when he was fitting and full of beauty, he changed and lost his beauty and became hateful.

3.18.4.en: And if you say: If He knew that he would change, why was He pleased with his temporary, unstable beauty?

3.18.5.en: Much can be said against these things; if love is present, hear it with discernment.

3.18.6.en: If the Examiner of all had acted according to His knowledge, He would have nullified the plan of the creative power.

3.18.7.en: He would not have brought Adam, whom He created, into Paradise, nor have commanded him not to eat of the tree (Gen 2:17).

3.18.8.en: Nor would He have created Satan with the angels, nor made the cunning serpent that deceived (Gen 3:1).

3.18.9.en: And the upright course of the creative power would have been halted, and the world would not have come into existence as it has.

3.18.10.en: If He had acted according to His knowledge, He would not have formed the blasphemer in his mother's womb.

3.18.11.en: Nor would He have given the pagan to see the light, nor brought the unbeliever into the world at all.

3.18.12.en: The One who knows all brought Himself down, as it were, to unknowing, for the sake of His many mercies toward His creation.

3.18.13.en: He molded Adam, knowing that he would not obey Him, and despite His knowledge He did not wish to annul (his creation) as the Knower.

3.18.14.en: He brought him into the garden, knowing that he would not remain in it, and by His good will He brought him in so that he might stay there.

3.18.15.en: He commanded him much not to eat of the tree, and had He acted according to His knowledge He would not have commanded him.

3.18.16.en: So also, although He knew that Satan would fall, He created him with the host of the heavenly ones.

3.18.17.en: He made for the unbeliever a mouth and a tongue, knowing that he would disbelieve in Him, and He did not deprive him of them.

3.18.18.en: The Lord brought Adam into the garden so that he might remain in the garden; but as for his leaving it after he sinned, that goes back to him.

3.18.19.en: He commanded him to keep himself from the tree, and since he did not keep himself as he was commanded, this goes back to his own will.

3.18.20.en: He created Satan with the host of the house of Michael so that he might praise Him, but he envied and fell from his freedom.

3.18.21.en: When our Lord chose Judas, knowing that he would betray Him, he also resembled his father in his works.

3.18.22.en: While he was beautiful He called him to the good tidings with the beautiful, and after he became abominable He mixed him with those who crucified.

3.18.23.en: His Father also does not reject people as long as they are beautiful, for He sent down fire upon Solomon's offering (2 Chr 7:1).

3.18.24.en: When (Solomon) was beautiful, He answered him in prayer and gave him fire, and after he became a servant of the pagan sacrifices, He cast him from Him(*) (1 Kgs 11).

3.18.25.en: The Son of God also promised Judas a throne (Mt 19:28), and because he denied Him, He brought him down and gave him the gallows as his wage (Mt 27:5)[9].

3.18.27.en: Raise up the wonderful temple of Your holiness within me!

3.18.28.en: v Allow me, O Heavenly One, to ask:

3.18.29.en: What were the feelings of the heavenly orders as they saw You become incarnate in the womb of the Virgin for my sake?

3.18.30.en: Are the heavens not pure before You, O Holy One?

3.18.31.en: Heaven and earth cannot contain You, O Unlimited One!

3.18.32.en: The heavenly ones are unable to comprehend Your surpassing mysteries!

3.18.33.en: How did You come down to our earth, You whom all the heavenly orders revere?

3.18.34.en: v You came down to us to raise from the earthly ones beings like the heavenly!

3.18.35.en: You raise us from the dunghill, and by Your Holy Spirit make us a temple for You!

3.18.36.en: v Solomon built You a temple on Mount Moriah, where Abraham offered his son Isaac to You as a burnt offering, in intention and love.

3.18.37.en: And David offered a sacrifice that You might forgive him, and rescue Your people from the plague!

3.18.38.en: And behold, You, the Lord of Solomon and his Savior, set up Your temple within me.

3.18.39.en: By Your Holy Spirit You turn my depths into a new Mount Moriah, and even make of my heart a wonderful Golgotha.

3.18.40.en: You declare the power of Your Cross and the joy of Your Resurrection within me!

3.18.41.en: v Solomon covered Your house with fir wood, with pure gold.

3.18.42.en: And behold, You clothe my heart with the incorruptible virginity, and turn my dust into a nature like the heavenly.

3.18.43.en: v Solomon garnished Your house with precious stones for beauty.

3.18.44.en: And behold, You adorn my soul by Your Holy Spirit, who grants me fellowship in the wonderful nature; by Your grace I become a living icon of You.

3.18.45.en: He takes of what is Yours and declares it to me.

3.18.46.en: He grants me love, joy, peace, chastity and goodness!

3.18.47.en: He shines in me with light, and dispels my darkness!

3.18.48.en: v It was not possible for any person to enter the Holy of Holies, except the high priest once a year.

3.18.49.en: Behold, You dwell in me, with Your heavenly Father and the Holy Spirit.

3.18.50.en: How great is Your love for humanity!

3.18.51.en: You raised her from her fall, and lifted her to surpassing glories.

3.18.52.en: You prepared her to enjoy sonship to You.

3.18.53.en: And behold, You prepare for her an inheritance that does not perish!

3.18.54.en: Grant that our hearts, minds, emotions and feelings become a chorus praising Your name without ceasing.

3.18.55.en: It shares the life of the heavenly orders.

3.18.56.en: What temple is this that is the work of Your hands?!
